definitions.definition: For natural j, c_j is the integer cast of Nat.choose(λ.toNat,j). For λ≥0 this is binom(λ,j).
D=∏_(t=0)^(λ.toNat) c_t; an empty product is one.

inputs.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.
For a prime p, a ring A with CharP A p, and n∈N, the element n! cast to A is a unit if and only if n<p.

hypotheses: p is a prime natural number.
A has characteristic p in the CharP sense.
source_contract.signature:
@IsUnit.natCast_factorial_iff_of_charP : ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring.{u_1} A] (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP.{u_1} A p] {n : ℕ},
  IsUnit.{u_1} ↑n.factorial ↔ LT.lt.{0} n p

inputs.statement: For natural numbers n,k with k≤n, choose(n,k)·k!·(n−k)!=n!.

hypotheses: n and k are natural numbers.

      n.factorial

output.statement: For every j with 0≤j≤λ the integer c_j=binom(λ,j) has nonzero image in K; for every r with 0≤r≤λ the integer r! has nonzero image in K. Hence D=∏_(j=0)^λ c_j also has nonzero image in K.

argument.text: For every natural r≤λ, H001 gives r<p. Apply M004 with ring K, its characteristic p from H001, and source natural n=r. The right side of its equivalence holds, so r! cast into K is a unit and hence nonzero in the field K. This includes r=0, whose factorial is one.

produces.statement: For every natural r≤λ, (r! in K) is nonzero.

argument.text: For every natural j≤λ, apply M005 with source n=λ.toNat and k=j. Cast its identity c_j j!(λ−j)!=λ! into K. Since λ! is nonzero by F001, the left side is nonzero; if c_j had zero image its product would be zero. Thus every c_j has nonzero image. A finite product of nonzero elements of a field is nonzero, by induction on the number of factors and the absence of zero divisors. D is precisely that product, so its image is nonzero. This proves the output statement with the factorial statement F001.
